key_insight: Removing viscous tilting of vorticity in DNS fundamentally alters turbulence structure, showing that viscosity-driven reorientation is essential to realistic Navier–Stokes turbulence.
engineering_relevance: Turbulence models and numerical solvers must capture viscous effects on vorticity orientation, because ignoring them can distort energy transfer and break the expected inertial-range scaling.
method: Directly modified direct numerical simulations of isotropic turbulence.
Surgically removed the viscous tilting term from vorticity evolution.
Compared flow structure and energy spectra against standard Navier–Stokes turbulence.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports a drastic flow-structure change and a substantial deviation from the -5/3 inertial-range energy spectrum when viscous tilting is removed in DNS.
watch_item: The intervention is highly idealized and specific to isotropic DNS, so generalization to complex flows or practical Reynolds numbers may require caution.
paper_title: Turbulence Without the Viscous Tilting of Vorticity
